title: Production Progressive Web App (PWA) with Workbox Service Worker, IndexedDB Offline Mutation Sync & Web Push Notifications
problem: Native mobile applications impose substantial distribution friction, lengthy app store review cycles, and large download sizes, while standard responsive web applications break entirely when network connectivity drops. Users in areas with intermittent mobile coverage lose unsaved form inputs, encounter browser dinosaur error pages, and miss critical real-time alerts. This project builds a production-grade Progressive Web App (PWA) in TypeScript and React. The system implements an app-shell architecture precached via Workbox Service Workers, stores application data and offline mutation queues in browser IndexedDB, synchronizes queued transactions in the background upon network reconnection using the Background Sync API, and delivers timely transactional alerts via the Web Push API with VAPID authentication.

use_cases.title: Field Technician Maintenance Logging & Work Orders
use_cases.first_sentence: Field service technicians inspecting remote wind turbines or basements frequently lose cellular signal while drafting maintenance reports.
use_cases.second_sentence: The PWA renders the precached app shell instantly offline, queues maintenance log submissions to IndexedDB, and automatically flushes queued updates to backend APIs once connectivity restores.

use_cases.title: Warehouse Logistics Barcode Scanning & Inventory Auditing
use_cases.first_sentence: Warehouse workers scanning physical inventory pallets in shielded distribution hubs need continuous UI responsiveness without network lag.
use_cases.second_sentence: The application persists inventory counts locally, updating quantities optimistically in the UI and synchronizing delta updates via background service worker sync.

use_cases.title: Emergency Dispatch & Public Safety Broadcast Alerts
use_cases.first_sentence: Municipal disaster relief teams require immediate real-time broadcast alerts on mobile web browsers even when the main app tab is closed.
use_cases.second_sentence: The service worker intercepts Web Push notifications using VAPID keys, rendering rich system notification badges and routing users to localized evacuation maps.

hard_parts: Designing cache invalidation and stale-while-revalidate routing strategies with Workbox to eliminate stale app-shell bundles without serving broken assets
Managing an append-only IndexedDB mutation queue that guarantees idempotent, FIFO transaction playback without duplicating orders upon reconnection
Handling browser Web Push subscription lifecycles, VAPID public/private key cryptographic verification, and push service endpoint changes
Architecting offline-first UI state synchronization in React that indicates network status changes with zero layout shift
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript and React codebase cleanly separating UI views, Workbox service worker routing, IndexedDB storage adapters, and Web Push managers
Lighthouse PWA audit achieving 100/100 PWA score and sub-1.2s First Contentful Paint (FCP) on simulated 4G mobile networks
Anti-fake verification script simulating complete browser offline mode (navigator.onLine=false), queuing an order in IndexedDB, and verifying automatic API commit upon reconnection

architecture.data_flow: The user loads the web app; the browser registers the Workbox service worker which precaches the app shell; user navigates between views; API data caches using a stale-while-revalidate strategy; if the device goes offline, network requests intercept and serve from IndexedDB or cache; when the user submits a form while offline, the payload writes to the IndexedDB mutation queue with a pending status and updates the UI optimistically; when network connectivity returns (via window online event or Background Sync), the service worker drains the queue in FIFO order, posts mutations to the backend API, and updates local record IDs; backend triggers Web Push events to display system notifications.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Idempotency keys on queued mutations preventing duplicate execution; cryptographic VAPID signatures validating push payloads.

targets.target: 50 of 50 offline mutations successfully synchronize with 0 duplicate submissions

riskiest_component.name: Stale Cache Traps and Broken Service Worker Update Cycles
riskiest_component.mitigation: Configure Workbox precache manifest revisions and implement skipWaiting prompt allowing users to activate new versions immediately.
riskiest_component.fallback: Hard-coded emergency unregister hook allowing client force-reload to clear corrupted service worker states.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a production Progressive Web App in TypeScript and React with Workbox service workers, IndexedDB offline sync, and Web Push.
worksheet.q2: Target users: mobile web application developers, frontend systems architects, and full-stack web engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: field technician maintenance logging, warehouse inventory auditing, and emergency dispatch broadcast alerts.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: Workbox cache invalidation strategies, IndexedDB FIFO transaction replay, VAPID push subscriptions, and offline UI state.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: React app scaffolding, Workbox config, IndexedDB sync helper, and mock API server. Synthetic data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Local VAPID keys generated via npm.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: stale cache traps in service worker. Fallback: precache manifest revisions and skipWaiting activation prompts.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: standard responsive web app without actual offline support. Anti-fake check 5 simulates offline disconnection and asserts IndexedDB queuing and sync.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic field inspection logs and local VAPID keys, zero personal data.
